long_biography.plain_text:
An F-16 pilot before entering the lawn-and-garden business, Jim Hagedorn brought an enduring interest in aviation to a career that shifted from sales and operations to corporate management. The family enterprise gave him an established starting platform, and its combination with a publicly traded peer retained a substantial family shareholding.

During his long tenure at Scotts Miracle-Gro, Hagedorn broadened the product portfolio through acquisitions of Ortho and Tomcat and pursued new consumer-marketing approaches. He held the chief executive post for roughly twenty-five years before a formal succession ended his management and board service. Away from the company, he has flown historic aircraft, including a P-51 Mustang.
